Performers
Symphony Orchestra (Gramophone Company) (orchestra), Albert Coates (conductor) Documented

The archive uploader calls the ensemble “Victor Symphony”. DAHR identifies the Gramophone Company Symphony Orchestra for the same matrix and catalogue issue; Victor is the American label, not sufficient evidence of a distinct orchestra.

[3] [2]
Work version
Four acoustic sides; precise cuts, performing edition and acoustic orchestration unestablished. Documented

The source describes the four-side acoustic issue. Its duration alone does not establish cuts or prove completeness. The guide does not label it an unabridged modern concert version. An orchestra animation is omitted because the acoustic scoring and exact alignment to the concert score have not been established.

[1] [2]
Recorded
28 April and 5 May 1922 Documented

Parts 1–⁠2: 28 April; Parts 3–⁠4: 5 May. The archive’s 1922-05-01 field is not accepted as an actual session date.

[2] [3]
Place
Hayes, Middlesex, England; Room 1 Documented

The room and locality are supplied by discographical records, not inferred from the later American issue.

[2] [3]
Label
Victor, American blue-label issue; corresponding HMV issues D670–D671 Documented

The archive identifies the transferred Victor discs; Bolig supplies the British catalogue equivalents.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
Victor 55176–⁠55177; HMV D670–D671 Documented

Bolig records North American issue in November 1922. The HMV equivalents are not substituted for the physical Victor carrier claimed by the upload.

[1] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
Part 1: Cc1260-3 (55176; D670; 3-0749). Part 2: Cc1261-3 (55176; D670; 3-0750). Part 3: Cc1262-3 (55177; D671; 3-0751). Part 4: Cc1293-2 (55177; D671; 3-0752). Documented

Issued takes and matrices come from Bolig’s Victor/HMV discography; Part 1 is corroborated by DAHR. They have not been read from run-out photographs of the discs used for this transfer.

[2] [3]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

Animating Apothecary Archives is identified as the upload source, not independently established as the transfer or mastering engineer.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Internet Archive upload date, 23 February 2023, is not a documented digitisation date.

[1]
Processing
The uploader reports some light filtering. Four issued sides are already joined in the supplied file. Documented

Filter settings, equipment, stylus, playback speed and any additional edits are not supplied; no further processing is inferred.

[1]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Strauss died in 1949. This term calculation does not clear an unidentified modern edition or assert worldwide status.

[6] [7]
Recording rights
Rule 2: American first publication in November 1922, within the programme’s 1925 cutoff. Documented

Bolig gives November 1922 for Victor 55176–⁠55177; his introduction explains that these issue months are drawn from North American supplements. The recording dates and the archive’s Public Domain Mark are corroborating context, not substitutes for publication evidence. No non-commercial condition is present on the supplied transfer.

[2] [3] [8]

Richard Strauss, Don Juan, Op. 20; Symphony Orchestra of the Gramophone Company, Albert Coates. Recorded at Hayes, 28 April and 5 May 1922; Victor 55176–⁠55177, issued November 1922. Transfer supplied by Animating Apothecary Archives via Internet Archive; engineer unidentified. Rights statement

  1. Internet Archive — Albert Coates, Don Juan, Victor 55176–⁠77, four sides — Item description and metadata: acoustic four-part transfer, Victor 12-inch blue-label discs, uploader and light filtering; file list supplies the MP3.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. John R. Bolig, The Victor Discography: Green, Blue, and Purple Labels (1909–⁠1930) — Printed pp. 163–⁠164: Victor 55176–⁠55177, Parts 1–⁠4, matrices/takes, recording dates, Hayes Room 1, HMV equivalents and November 1922 issue. Printed p. xv explains that italic issue months refer to North American monthly supplements.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Discography of American Historical Recordings — Cc1260, Don Juan Part 1 — Gramophone Company Symphony Orchestra, Albert Coates; master take 3, 28 April 1922, Hayes Room 1; Victor 55176 and HMV D670/3-0749.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Richard Strauss critical edition — Don Juan introduction — PDF pp. 1–⁠5 (printed XI–XV): Lenau, dedication to Thuille, autograph completion 30 September 1888, Weimar première 11 November 1889, early reception and orchestral writing. Preferred over retrospective anecdotes about the first ideas arising in Italy.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Herbert Glass — Don Juan, LA Phil programme note — Opening flourish, unison horn idea, extended wind melody, Lenau and Hanslick’s 1890 criticism. Programme-note interpretation is distinguished from recording-specific timing.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Gerald Larner — Don Juan, tone poem, Op. 20 — Composer dates 1864–⁠1949; structural sequence, lyrical episodes, E-major recapitulation and E-minor coda. Its retrospective composition anecdote is not adopted over the critical edition.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Directive 2006/116/EC — copyright term — Articles 1 and 8: ordinary life-plus-70 term and calculation from the next January.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. 17 U.S.C. § 1401 — pre-1972 sound recordings — Section (a)(2), including first publication before 1923; used with the programme’s historical-recording cutoff.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
